questions.subtopic: Case Study 2: Land Degradation in India
questions.question: Case Study 2 (Continued): Industrial effluents have become a major source of land and water pollution in many parts of India.\n\nQ15: What is the most effective method for controlling land degradation caused by industrial waste?
options: Proper treatment and safe disposal of industrial effluents and wastes before discharging them into water bodies or dumping on land
Dumping all factory waste into active volcanoes
Shipping all industrial waste to Antarctica
Banning all electricity usage in factories
questions.explanation: Establishing effluent treatment plants (ETPs) and recycling toxic chemical waste prior to release prevents toxic chemicals from poisoning surrounding soils and aquifers.

questions.subtopic: Case Study 2: Land Degradation in India
questions.question: Case Study 2 (Continued): In dry and desert regions of western India:\n\nQ16: Which biological conservation method is used to stabilize shifting sand dunes?
options: Paving the entire desert with tarmac
Covering the desert with plastic tarpaulins
Flooding the desert with seawater
Planting thorny bushes and rows of shelter trees
questions.explanation: Planting drought-resistant thorny shrubs and establishing rows of shelter belt trees anchors loose desert sand dunes and checks windblown sand encroachment.

questions.subtopic: Case Study 3: The Alluvial Soils of India
questions.question: How have the fertile alluvial plains of northern India supported dense settlement and intensive agriculture?
options: Because alluvial regions are the only places where gold is found
Because alluvial soils have no summer heat
Because the government provides free housing on alluvial plains
Their fertile soils, relatively level terrain and river-water availability support productive agriculture and settlement
questions.explanation: The fertile alluvial plains, level terrain and river-water availability have supported intensive agriculture and dense settlement. The revised wording avoids implying that every area with alluvial soil is among India’s most densely populated places.

questions.subtopic: Case Study 3: The Alluvial Soils of India
questions.question: Case Study 3 (Continued): Apart from the northern plains, where else are significant expanses of alluvial soils found in peninsular India?

On top of the Anamudi peak in Western Ghats
In the core of the Thar desert
Across the Malwa plateau
questions.explanation: The eastern coastal plains, especially the fertile delta regions of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri rivers, are covered with rich alluvial deposits.

questions.subtopic: Case Study 4: Soil Erosion and Conservation in Chambal
questions.question: Case Study 4 (Q19-Q20): Soil erosion in the Chambal basin has created a famous landscape of badlands known as ravines.\n\nQ19: Which primary form of soil erosion has sculpted the Chambal ravines?
options: Wind erosion blowing away sand
Glacial plucking by mountain ice
Gully erosion caused by deep downcutting of running water in clayey soil
Coastal marine wave erosion
questions.explanation: The Chambal ravines are a classic example of badland topography produced by gully erosion: running water cuts deep channels into the terrain. The explanation avoids asserting a specific underlying alluvial composition where the question only requires the erosion process.

questions.subtopic: Case Study 4: Soil Erosion and Conservation in Chambal
questions.question: Case Study 4 (Continued): To reclaim ravines and prevent further gully erosion in undulating landscapes:\n\nQ20: What engineering and vegetative measures are recommended by soil conservationists?
options: Blasting all ravines with dynamite
Constructing check dams across gullies, terracing, contour trenching, and extensive afforestation of catchment areas
Paving gullies with concrete
Diverting the entire Chambal river into the Arabian Sea
questions.explanation: Building small check dams traps silt, halts further channel deepening, and allows planted tree roots and grasses to stabilize the ravine slopes.
